clue.text: Keeping well in San Sebastian, Dawn (with hairdo) looks refreshed? Say no more

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the rearranged letters hold the other word inside them
something refreshed has been done up anew, so these letters are given a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder
well and good both mean satisfactory, as in 'all is well'

annotation.spelling: A NOD'S AS GOOD AS A WINK TO A BLIND HORSE

explanation.surface: A woman on holiday in San Sebastian, feeling well, looks revived after a new hairdo.
explanation.walkthrough: All 27 letters of San Sebastian, Dawn, hairdo and looks are rearranged around GOOD, which stays intact in the middle of the proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb means a hint is enough and nothing further need be spelt out, which is what 'say no more' conveys.

clue.text: Song by leaderless congregation in bubble

indicators.note: without a leader means the word loses its front letter

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
a church congregation is a priest's flock

explanation.surface: A hymn sung by a congregation that has lost its minister, cocooned in its own bubble.
explanation.definitionFit: An airlock is a bubble of trapped air that blocks the flow of liquid in a pipe.

clue.text: Love, pleasurable, temporarily put aside

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
nice means pleasant or pleasurable

explanation.surface: A pleasant romance that has been paused for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan kept on ice is idiomatically postponed, held in reserve rather than abandoned.

clue.text: Appearing in tabloid: it's a knitted bear!

indicators.note: to appear in a newspaper is to sit within its pages, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper

indicators.note: knitting works strands into a new form, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A tabloid runs a story about a knitted teddy bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' at the end looks like the knitted toy, but it is the verb meaning to carry or endure.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain a weight or a loss is to bear it, the two verbs being synonyms.

clue.text: Czech composer in Paris met an arranger

indicators.note: in tells you the name sits inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across the end of Paris, all of met and an, and the start of arranger

explanation.surface: A Czech composer meets someone in Paris who will arrange his music.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedřich Smetana was a nineteenth-century Czech composer, best known for Má vlast and The Bartered Bride.

clue.text: When guards live and perish showing duty

indicators.note: a guard surrounds what it protects, so one word wraps around the others

parts.note: once means when, as in 'once you arrive'
to be is to exist or live
to perish is to die

explanation.surface: Guards who are prepared to live or die in service demonstrate their sense of duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Obedience, doing what one is told, is a form of dutifulness, so duty is a loose synonym.

clue.text: Boozer, the German circles skating arena

indicators.note: to circle something is to go around it, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: der is a German word for 'the'
an ice rink is where people skate

explanation.surface: A German drunk staggers around and around an ice rink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' is also British slang for a pub, but here it means the person who drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinker, in the sense of a heavy one, is a boozer: both name someone fond of alcohol.

clue.text: Snacks made by Schwarzenegger aboard ship?

indicators.note: to be aboard is to be on a ship, so the name goes inside the ship's abbreviation

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
Arnie is the nickname of Arnold Schwarzenegger

explanation.surface: Arnold Schwarzenegger making snacks in a ship's galley.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarnie is British slang for a sandwich, and sandwiches are snacks.

clue.text: Keep up check on page in article by expert

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the pair of words that follows it

parts.note: to stay something is to check or halt it, as in a stay of execution
the is the definite article
P is the abbreviation for page
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: An expert checks a page of an article before publication.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the word for check comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay the pace is idiomatically to keep up with others and not fall behind.

clue.text: Mournful echo in Gaelic ground

parts.note: Echo is E in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so these letters are broken up and remixed

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A sorrowful echo resounds across Gaelic land.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegiac describes the tone of an elegy, a lament for the dead, so it means sorrowful.

clue.text: Almost crossing oceans when fishing restricted?

indicators.note: crossing means spanning from one side to the other, so the phrase stretches around the other word

parts.note: close on means almost, as in close on a hundred
the seas are the oceans

explanation.surface: Trawlers nearly crossing the oceans while fishing is limited.
explanation.walkthrough: The two-word phrase for almost splits around the oceans.
explanation.definitionFit: The close season is the part of the year when fishing or hunting a species is banned by law.

clue.text: Sailor leaving shellfish for sole

indicators.note: when someone leaves, they are no longer there, so those letters drop out of the longer word

parts.note: the abalone is an edible sea snail with a pearly shell
AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor turns down shellfish and orders sole instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' looks like the fish, continuing the seafood menu, but it means only.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole and alone both mean single, without anyone else, as in the sole survivor.

clue.text: See 1
Admitted being deceived?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: allowed inside, given shelter

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as someone confessing they were fooled; the two halves are separate meanings of one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A lodger is taken in when admitted to a house; a dupe is taken in when tricked.

clue.text: Sedaka maybe carrying on, average or unequalled?

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it, so the name holds the other words inside it

parts.note: Neil Sedaka is an American singer-songwriter; maybe marks him as one example of a Neil
taken as written
par is the standard or average level

explanation.surface: Asks whether singer Neil Sedaka is merely middling or without equal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonpareil, from French, means having no equal: matchless or peerless.

clue.text: Area where gibbon lives: no place for 24?

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area
a gibbon is an ape that lives in a tree

explanation.surface: Describes a zoo enclosure where a gibbon lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 is the end of the long proverb, A BLIND HORSE. Aintree is the Liverpool racecourse that hosts the Grand National steeplechase, with its huge fences.
explanation.definitionFit: A course of big jumps is no place for a horse that cannot see, so the cross-reference cryptically defines the racecourse.

clue.text: Energy in peanut, crushed and devoured

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the rearranged word
crushed means pounded out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Energy-rich peanuts were ground down and swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been eaten up has been consumed completely, which is to be devoured.

clue.text: Sinatra plays for leading lady

indicators.note: to play with something is to toy with it, so these letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Frank Sinatra performs opposite a leading lady in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading lady' suggests a star actress, but here it is the woman leading a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the empress of Russia, a woman at the head of the country.

clue.text: Glib talk used by new model

parts.note: patter is a smooth, rapid line of talk, like a salesman's
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking line spun by a new fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern is a model or template to be copied, as in a dressmaking pattern.

clue.text: Absolve Gaunt beginning to suffer in church

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
gaunt means thin or lean

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of suffer

explanation.surface: A haggard sinner seeks absolution and begins to suffer penance in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gaunt' looks like a name (John of Gaunt), but it is the adjective thin.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse someone of sin is to purify them, which is what absolving does.

clue.text: Fast runner no sporting sort did you say?

indicators.note: asking whether you said it points to how a word is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a cheater is an unsporting person who breaks the rules

explanation.surface: Asks whether a fast runner is in fact a cheat.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is the fastest land animal, a big cat that sprints after prey.

clue.text: Dicky in US having drink with Bond?

parts.note: to neck a drink is British slang for swallowing it fast
a tie is a bond or connection

explanation.surface: Pictures James Bond with a drink, wearing a dicky bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' suggests 007, but it is a plain noun. A dicky (dicky bow) is British for a bow tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Necktie is the American word for a tie worn around the collar, covering the item the British call a dicky.

clue.text: Queen's classic visit to 14?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the 1976 album by the rock band Queen
second meaning: an outing to the racecourse at 14-across

explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' looks like the monarch, who loves horse racing; it is the band. 'Classic' also hints at the Classics, Britain's five top flat races.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a Queen album and also describes a trip to Aintree racecourse.

clue.text: See 20
Man I have heard on the radio?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a man's first name

definitions.text: I have heard on the radio
definitions.meaning: second meaning: radio procedure word for message received

explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' tempts a solver to look for a sound-alike, but it is part of the radio meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: In radio voice procedure the word signals 'received and understood', and it is also a common male name.

clue.text: Sinister look from Levi troubled detective

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so these letters are thrown out of their order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
a private eye is a detective

explanation.surface: A worried man called Levi gets a menacing stare from a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: The evil eye is a malevolent glare believed to cast a curse, so a sinister look.

clue.text: Superman reportedly getting cramp?

indicators.note: reportedly means as told by word of mouth, so go by the spoken sound

parts.note: a titan is a person of superhuman strength or stature

explanation.surface: Superman suffering a muscle cramp, according to reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cramp' looks like the noun for a muscle spasm, but it is the verb meaning to restrict.
explanation.definitionFit: To cramp is to confine or constrict, as does tightening something.
